name: Frontier
comment: Frontier is a HPE Cray EX exascale supercomputer at OLCF. With a theoretical peak double-precision performance of approximately 2 exaflops (2 quintillion calculations per second), it is the fastest system in the world for a wide range of traditional computational science applications. The system has 77 Olympus rack HPE cabinets, each with 128 AMD compute nodes, and a total of 9,856 AMD compute nodes. Source: https://docs.olcf.ornl.gov/systems/frontier_user_guide.html

parts.name: Frontier Compute Partition
parts.comment: 77 Olympus rack cabinets x 128 nodes each = 9,856 compute nodes. Source: https://docs.olcf.ornl.gov/systems/frontier_user_guide.html

power_draw_peak.comment: approximate; OLCF reports total facility power but exact peak compute power not publicly documented

bandwidth.comment: 8 channels x 25.6 GB/s = 204.8 GB/s theoretical peak

memory.comment: 512 GB DDR4 per node with 4 NUMA domains. Source: https://docs.olcf.ornl.gov/systems/frontier_user_guide.html

accelerators.name: Instinct MI250X

amount.comment: HBM2E per GCD (compute die); 2 GCDs per MI250X = 128 GB per MI250X card

tdp.comment: From AMD website; base TDP, not peak

accelerators.comment: Each MI250X has 2 Graphics Compute Dies (GCDs); the 8 GCDs per node appear as 8 separate GPUs to Slurm and ROCm

node_types.comment: 9,856 identical compute nodes. 56 allocatable cores per node (8 reserved: 1 core per L3 region for system processes and SLURM core specialization). Source: https://docs.olcf.ornl.gov/systems/frontier_user_guide.html
